title: Handover
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/dispatches/<dispatch_id>/handover, application/json: the starter asks for the run key and the input of the job it started for the dispatch. Before calling handover, the starter has satisfied itself that the job asking is the one it started for this dispatch. It passes the run key to that job alone, and keeps it no longer than that. How it proves the job is the starter's business. For a dispatched run, the handover is the run's registration, https://qory.dev/contracts/forager/v1/run-registration.schema.json: the control plane registers the run, as a registration through a gateway by the node pool, when it answers the handover, and the answer's run_key is that registered run's run key, bound to the claimed run and to the gateway the node pool's choice resolved to, as the run key's run_id and gateway name them. The job never registers a dispatched run itself. The control plane refuses, under any key, a registration at the run endpoint whose run_id is that of a run of this contract, waiting for a node pool, claimed, handed over or ended, with the signed 409 run_id_used, decided first: before the stored answer to a repeated registration and before the instance limit. The Forager contract gives the run endpoint's other causes and their order. So a dispatched run's run key comes only from the handover. What a registration would carry, the run's id, its labels, what it is about and its attach window, the control plane sets from the dispatch, the run's id being the claimed run's run_id. The registered run's instance id, the run key's instance_id, is the run's id, the claimed run_id, so each dispatched run is a new instance, which holds the slot of the pool's instance limit it took at the claim, claim.schema.json. A run key is handed over at most once per run: the answer, handover-answer.schema.json, is given once, sent with Cache-Control: no-store and never cached, and a second handover while the run goes on is refused, 409 handed_over, in the order below. The control plane registers the run, issues its run key and moves the dispatch to handed over as one step, so of two concurrent handovers of a dispatch, one is answered the signed 200 and the other is refused, 409 handed_over. Once a dispatch's handover is answered, its run never goes back to the queue, and the dispatch ends with its run: a release after it ends the run, release.schema.json. A dispatch_id that is unknown, or of another node pool than the key's, is refused 403 forbidden, with the same signed body either way, so nobody learns whether an id exists. The signature with the pool's access key and that check authorise the request, not the id. When a dispatch's handover has not been answered before lease_until, its lease lapses: at or after lease_until, its run goes back to the queue with the same run_id, and the dispatch is stale: it is never handed over, and it ends with its run. A dispatched, handover or release naming a stale dispatch is refused 409 lease_expired while its run has not ended, and 410 gone once it has, for example because its work item was closed or undone while the run waited, or because the run ended under a later dispatch; a handover is refused 409 handed_over instead when its run was handed over through a later dispatch, as the order below gives. A handover is refused for the first of these that applies, in this order: 403 forbidden, as above; 410 gone, the dispatch ended, as refusal.schema.json describes, so a run that was handed over and then ended answers 410 gone; 409 handed_over, the run was handed over before, through this or any other dispatch; 409 lease_expired, the dispatch is stale, and the starter then stops the job it started for that dispatch; 409 not_dispatched, the handover came before dispatched, dispatched.schema.json; 409 no_gateway, the node pool has no gateway the run could be registered through: its choice is direct, its choice is the default and no default gateway resolves for its workspace, its named gateway may no longer serve its workspace, or the gateway its choice resolves to has no active access key (the Forager contract's choice direct and its codes no_default_gateway, gateway_not_serving and gateway_without_key); 503 unavailable, the control plane failed to make the run's inputs or its run key. After a 409 no_gateway, the dispatch stays claimed until its lease lapses, so the starter may send the handover again, built anew, while the lease lasts; after that, 409 lease_expired applies. A 503 unavailable is signed, and the handover took no effect, since it is one step: no run is registered, no run key is issued, and the dispatch is left as it was, dispatched and not handed over, so the starter may send the handover again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff, while the lease lasts; after that, 409 lease_expired applies. A refused handover registers no run and takes no new slot of the pool's instance limit: the dispatch keeps the slot it took at the claim until that slot is freed. It is signed with the pool's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the starter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.
